newsitem.title: USA: ITT seeks partner for SEAT SpA bid. [CORRECTED 16:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: ITT seeks partner for SEAT SpA bid. [CORRECTED 16:55 GMT]

text.p: ITT Corp said Friday it would seek a partner if it was successful in its bid to acquire Italy's SEAT SpA, a telephone directory business.
"We never had the intention of footing the bill alone," said ITT spokesman Jim Gallagher. "We have some partners in mind.
"Our plan was to get down to the short strokes and then make our final bid. Our plan was that our bid would be part of a consortium."
He declined to identify any potential partners.
ITT, one of a handful of remaining SEAT bidders, said that in the acquisition it would spend no more than one-tenth of the value of the directory business over several years.
Gallagher confirmed reports that SEAT's value was near $1.6 billion.
He said the acquisition would be "significantly accretive" to ITT.
"It is an extremely valuable piece of property. We would have been derelict in our duties had we not bid on SEAT," he said.
When ITT rejected Hilton Hotels Corp's $6.5 billion takeover offer last week, it said it planned to focus on its core business of casinos and hotels.
Gallagher said the SEAT bid does not depart from that plan.
"It in no way signals a change in our very specific direction that we announced in rejecting the Hilton offer," he said.

ITT said it is considering selling its World Directories unit as part of its plan to shed non-core assets. (Corrects to show sale of unit is being considered but has not been decided.) It said the acquisition of SEAT would enhance the value of the directories unit.
"It makes ITT directories significantly more valuable, whether we plan to own it or someone else owns it," Gallagher said.
